name: Last Air-Cooled
tagline: The last air-cooled 911, and a modern classic
description: The 993 was built from January 1994 to March 1998 as the fourth 911 and the last air-cooled Porsche. Tony Hatter’s redesign kept the silhouette but added flatter polyellipsoid headlights, integrated bumpers and a new LSA (Light, Stable, Agile) aluminium chassis with a multi-link rear axle that cured lift-off oversteer; only about a fifth of the parts carried over from the 964. The engine line ran from a 272 PS 3.6-litre flat-six to the 285 PS VarioRam car and the first biturbo 911, a 408 PS twin-turbo. The range widened into Carrera 4S and Carrera S, the 300 PS Carrera RS, the rear-drive GT2, the 450 PS Turbo S, plus rare Speedster and Turbo Cabriolet specials. Road production ended on 31 March 1998, and today the 993 is widely treated as the most desirable post-classic 911.

variants.name: 911 Carrera
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled flat-six, twin-spark, VarioRam from 1996
variants.description: The 993 Carrera opened the fourth generation in January 1994 as the lightest and purest of the range. Its 3.6-litre air-cooled flat-six kept the 964's bore and stroke but gained twin-spark ignition, a dual-flow exhaust with two catalytic converters and, from model year 1996, the VarioRam variable-length intake that lifted output from 272 to 285 PS. A six-speed manual was standard — a 911 first — with a four-speed Tiptronic optional. Tony Hatter's smoothed, polyellipsoid-headlamp body rode on the new LSA aluminium chassis with its multi-link Weissach rear axle. Around 23,000 Coupés were built, making this the volume 993.

variants.name: 911 Carrera 4
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled flat-six, twin-spark, VarioRam from 1996
variants.description: For model year 1995 the Carrera 4 brought all-wheel drive back on a lighter, simpler system: a viscous multi-plate clutch replaced the 964's three-differential layout, a layout descended from the 959 that still sent most torque rearward. Output came from the same 3.6-litre flat-six, 272 PS rising to 285 PS with VarioRam for 1996. Visual tells are easy — clear front indicators, red rears, silver calipers and Carrera 4 wheel caps. At 1,420 kg it is roughly 50 kg heavier than the rear-drive Carrera, and Tiptronic was not offered. Coupé and Cabriolet bodies both sold.

variants.name: 911 Carrera 4S
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64.21 naturally aspirated flat-six with VarioRam
variants.description: Introduced for model year 1996, the Carrera 4S put the wide 911 Turbo bodyshell — with its Turbo-derived suspension, lowered stance and 322 mm cross-drilled four-piston brakes — under a naturally aspirated engine. It keeps all-wheel drive, unlike the later Carrera S, and omits the Turbo's fixed wing, retaining only the electrically extending Carrera spoiler. With 285 PS through a six-speed manual it is the heavier of the wide-body pair at 1,450 kg. The very last air-cooled 911 built for the road, completed on 31 March 1998, was a Riviera Blue Carrera 4S.

variants.name: 911 Carrera S
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64.21 naturally aspirated flat-six with VarioRam
variants.description: The Carrera S arrived for model year 1997 as the rear-drive answer to the 4S: the same Turbo-sourced wide body and front panel, but without the all-wheel-drive hardware or the Turbo's 322 mm brakes. Output stayed at 285 PS from the 3.6-litre VarioRam flat-six, routed through a six-speed manual or Tiptronic S. Production ran to roughly 3,700 cars worldwide — most destined for North America — and a handful of Cabriolets were hand-built through Porsche Exclusiv although never catalogued. Enthusiasts call it the 2S, and it is today among the most valuable standard-body 993s.

variants.name: 911 Targa
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled flat-six with VarioRam
variants.description: The 993 Targa, launched for model year 1996, reinvented the badge. Instead of a removable roof panel and a wide roll-over hoop, a large electrically operated laminated-glass panel slid beneath the steeply raked rear screen, leaving the Carrera profile untouched and flooding the cabin with light. The old B-pillar hoop disappeared entirely, though the mechanism added weight high up and proved more complex than a simple lift-off panel. Built on the Cabriolet structure and identified by distinctive two-piece 17-inch wheels, it used the 285 PS VarioRam engine with rear-wheel drive and optional Tiptronic S. About 4,600 were made.

variants.name: 911 Cabriolet
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled flat-six, twin-spark, VarioRam from 1996
variants.drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive (all-wheel drive available as Carrera 4 Cabriolet)
variants.description: Revealed alongside the Coupé in April 1994 for the 1995 model year, the 993 Cabriolet wore a fully electrical, hand-stitched soft top reinforced with metal panels, an automatic wind blocker and a small rear spoiler carrying the third brake light. It shares the Coupé's 3.6-litre flat-six — 272 PS, then 285 PS with VarioRam — and its six-speed manual or Tiptronic, and was also offered with all-wheel drive as the Carrera 4 Cabriolet. At about 1,390 kg it is only a little heavier than the Coupé. A large share of the roughly 15,500 Cabriolets built went to the United States.

variants.name: 911 Turbo
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64/60 twin-turbocharged air-cooled flat-six, air-to-air intercooled
variants.description: In 1995 the 911 Turbo entered its twin-turbo era. Two small KKK turbochargers spooling from about 2,000 rpm gave the 3.6-litre flat-six 408 PS and 540 Nm with far less lag than a single large unit, at 0.8 bar of boost. It was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, simplified from the 959, and the first production car in the world with OBD-II diagnostics — its engine also had the lowest emissions of any series-production unit at the time. Wide rear arches, a fixed intercooler wing and hollow-spoke 18-inch wheels marked it out. A six-speed manual was standard; 5,978 were built.

variants.name: 911 Turbo S
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 twin-turbocharged air-cooled flat-six, larger Triple K K-24 turbos
variants.power: 450 PS (331 kW) Euro; 424 hp (316 kW) US
variants.description: The Turbo S was Porsche Exclusive's 1997–98 farewell to the air-cooled Turbo. Larger Triple K K-24 turbochargers, an extra oil cooler and reworked Motronic management lifted output to 450 PS in European trim, 424 hp for the United States. It is unmistakable: yellow brake calipers, a biplane Aerokit II wing, quad exhaust tips, brake-duct intakes where the fog lamps used to be, and the 993 Turbo's first rear-quarter side scoops. Leather and carbon trim covered nearly every interior surface, in contrast to the spartan 964 Turbo S. Around 345 were built — the last air-cooled 911 Turbo, and among the rarest series 993s.

variants.name: 911 Carrera RS
variants.engine: 3.75 L M64/20 naturally aspirated flat-six (3,746 cc), VarioRam, twin oil coolers
variants.description: The Carrera RS of 1995–96 was the last air-cooled Rennsport 911 and the last to carry 'Carrera' in its RS title. Its 3.8-litre flat-six used VarioRam, forged pistons, big intake valves and a revised Motronic for 300 PS, driving a close-ratio six-speed with a single-mass flywheel. The body was seam-welded, lightened with an aluminium bonnet and thinner glass, stripped of sound deadening and set on Bilstein dampers under three-piece 18-inch wheels. A fixed wing, front lip and brake-cooling inlets replaced the standard rear seat and headlamp washers. Just 1,014 were built — and it was never approved for the United States.

variants.name: 911 Carrera RS Clubsport
variants.engine: 3.75 L M64/20 naturally aspirated flat-six (3,746 cc), VarioRam
variants.description: The M003 Clubsport option turned the Carrera RS into a road-legal track tool. A welded roll cage, suspension strut brace, composite buckets with six-point harnesses, battery cut-off and fire extinguisher went in; carpets, electric windows, air-conditioning and the radio came out. A larger biplane wing and deeper chin spoiler replaced the Touring aero, and fourth through sixth gears were shortened. Otherwise it matched the standard RS: 300 PS from 3.8 litres, 322 mm cross-drilled Turbo brakes, Bilstein dampers and a limited-slip differential. Of the 1,014 RS cars built, 227 left the factory as Clubsports. Like the RS, it was never sold in the United States.

variants.name: 911 GT2
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64/60R twin-turbocharged air-cooled flat-six, raised boost
variants.description: Racing rules banning all-wheel drive turned the 993 Turbo into the rear-drive GT2, homologated for the FIA GT2 class and badged simply '911 GT' on the decklid. Bolt-on plastic arches, a strut-mounted wing with integrated air scoops and a stripped RS-style cabin defined it; the biturbo ran higher boost for 430 PS, rising to 450 PS for 1998 with dual ignition. Roughly 200 kg lighter than the Turbo, it was the most extreme road 993 — 0–100 km/h in under four seconds and a 296 km/h top speed. Around 57 were sold for homologation alongside some 110 customer racers.

variants.name: 911 GT2 Evo
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64/83 twin-turbocharged flat-six, larger KKK K27 turbos, 40.4 mm restrictors
variants.power: 600 PS (441 kW) @ 7,000 rpm in GT1 race trim; 450 PS road-spec Evolution
variants.description: To take the GT2 into FIA GT1, Porsche built the GT2 Evo. A larger KKK K27 turbocharger set with 40.4 mm restrictors, a redesigned intake and exhaust, and optimized internals lifted the 3.6-litre flat-six to 600 PS, while the body gained an even higher rear wing, wider arches for GT1 tyres and extra cooling ducts; weight fell to about 1,100 kg. Production was tiny — nine to eleven race cars depending on the source — and a separate run of 21 road-legal Evolution cars at 450 PS is also recorded. The Evo was overtaken by the mid-engined 911 GT1.

variants.name: 911 Speedster
variants.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled flat-six (Carrera 3.6 as built)
variants.description: Porsche never catalogued a 993 Speedster. Two were built by Porsche Exclusive: a dark green Tiptronic S car with 17-inch wheels for Ferdinand Alexander Porsche's 60th birthday in 1995, and a wide-body, 18-inch manual car for Jerry Seinfeld, converted from a Cabriolet in 1998. Both use the 3.6-litre Carrera flat-six with the roof chopped down and a redesigned interior; a few more Cabriolets were converted by outside coachbuilders. A third claim of a 2000 build appears in Porsche's own Exclusive history. Factory performance, weight and torque figures were never published, so those fields are left empty rather than guessed.

variants.name: 911 Turbo Cabriolet
variants.engine: 3.6 L single-turbocharged flat-six from the 964 Turbo 3.6
variants.description: Before the twin-turbo Coupé arrived, Porsche Exclusive quietly built fourteen 993 Turbo Cabriolets during 1995. Each carried the 360 PS single-turbo 3.6-litre engine and five-speed manual gearbox of the 964 Turbo 3.6, rear-wheel drive, and that car's fixed rear wing, mounted on the open 993 body. At DM 89,500 — a 62 per cent premium over a standard 993 Cabriolet — they were among the priciest 993s of all. No official weight, acceleration or top-speed figures were ever published, so those fields stay empty rather than invented. Fourteen cars makes it one of the rarest 993 variants.
